orders.name: Progress note
orders.detail: MFM Consultation: Acute Hemolytic Anemia in Pregnancy

GUI.note:
Assessment
27-year-old G1 at 26 weeks gestation of Sardinian (Italian) ancestry with known beta thalassemia minor (baseline Hb 10.6 g/dL, MCV 64 fL, ferritin 46 ng/mL, HbA2 5.1%) presenting with an acute fall in hemoglobin from 10.6 to 7.8 g/dL (MCV rose from 64 to 69 fL), fatigue, scleral icterus/jaundice, dark cola-colored urine, elevated LDH (538 U/L), and elevated unconjugated bilirubin (total 3.1 mg/dL, direct 0.3 mg/dL) with normal platelets (228), ALT (18), and creatinine (0.6).

1. Cause of New Anemia: The acute drop in hemoglobin is NOT explained by her baseline beta thalassemia trait or iron deficiency. Rather, it is caused by a new process: acute drug-induced oxidative hemolytic anemia triggered by nitrofurantoin (100 mg BID prescribed on 2024-05-21 by obstetric triage for asymptomatic bacteriuria), due to underlying glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency (Mediterranean variant strongly associated with Sardinian ancestry, co-inherited with beta thalassemia trait).
2. Untreated Infection: Incompletely treated Escherichia coli (>100,000 CFU/mL) asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy, as the patient self-discontinued nitrofurantoin after 3 days due to dark urine
